elements.text: Flight crew's failure to identify and arrest the helicopter's descent
Flight crew's failure to identify and arrest the helicopter's descent for undetermined reasons
Controlled flight into terrain
Captain and copilot were properly certificated and qualified
No evidence of medical or behavioral conditions affecting performance
Flight crew fatigue was not a factor
Helicopter was properly certified, equipped, and maintained
No evidence of structural, engine, or system failures in recovered components
Weather was not a factor
Dispatcher provided appropriate flight-tracking services
Search and rescue effort was timely
Accident was not survivable due to impact forces exceeding human tolerance limits
Few, if any, visual references available outside the helicopter despite VMC
Helicopter crashed into water at high airspeed, shallow descent angle, and near-level roll attitude
Pilots were not attempting an emergency landing on the water
Fuselage pitched nose down and tailboom broke off after crash
Flight crew was not adequately monitoring altitude
Flight crew missed numerous cues indicating inadvertent descent toward water
Lack of terrain awareness and warning system prevented timely recognition of descent
Recommendation for additional pilot training on SPZ-7000 and SPZ-7600 systems
Recommendation for ADS-B technology to mitigate offshore risks
Recommendation for preflight testing and maintenance of CVR
FAA exemption from flight data recorder requirements hampered investigation
